questions.title: General law regulating the Egyptian medical profession
questions.question: One of the following is a General Law that regulates the Egyptian medical profession:

options.C: Law No. 415/1954 for practice of the medical profession

explanations.A: Correct. The Penal Code is a GENERAL law — it applies to everyone and to all conduct, including doctors, and so it is one of the general laws that regulate the medical profession. General laws are distinguished from special (specific) laws that are written to govern a particular activity. Because the Penal Code governs criminal liability for all citizens, it counts as a general law bearing on medical practice.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The Profession Ethics Regulations 238/2003 are a special regulation issued specifically for the medical profession, not a general law.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Law No. 415/1954 for the practice of the medical profession is the classic SPECIAL law governing medical practice specifically, not a general law.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Option A (the Penal Code) is a valid general law, so 'none of the above' is wrong.

questions.subtopic: Egyptian Medical Syndicate and the regulation of practice
questions.learning_objective: Distinguish general laws (e.g. the Penal Code) from special laws (Law 415/1954) regulating the Egyptian medical profession.
